rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module prerequisite rescue: run it late, never fabricate
rules_evaluated.evidence: The existing 'artefact is whatever's there... open a fresh Claude Code session... ask it to read what the M4 run touched' rescue (Push-back moves + Per-phase table, unchanged by this diff) answers 'is the repo state reachable', not 'is the M4 SESSION itself still alive' -- and the new '## Say what done-done means' section (added since @ba5ccf5, line 26) specifically needs the latter: its prompt fence is prefaced 'This one runs in the session you sent off. Its answer lands in the transcript you are about to read' (line 30) and the prompt itself (curriculum/prompts/ae101-m5-done-done.md) asks Claude to 'Answer per point, with evidence from THIS SESSION.' Prework (line 8, unchanged) explicitly pre-authorizes exactly the failure case that breaks this: 'Walk in with your un-packaged session. Stopped, finished, ran out of credit, doesn't matter.' training-architecture.md's canonical session-boundary text (Section boundaries, unchanged) states cross-module continuity 'lives on disk... not in chat history' and its own return verb's fallback is 'if it is not still open, start a fresh one' -- but a fresh session has no real per-point evidence to offer, so if a student runs this prompt in a fresh session (the only rescue named anywhere in the file), the agent is asked to answer 'with evidence from this session' about a session it was never part of -- inviting exactly the confabulated, plausible-but-wrong self-report the module's own Phase 1 later teaches the student to distrust. No body text or maintainer note names this narrower failure or gives it a recovery move; the existing Connections-blocker push-back (written before this section existed) doesn't cover it because it answers a different question.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Narrow, not a restatement of the whole return architecture (per §64): one clause on the prompt's own precondition would do it -- e.g. 'if that session's gone, tell the fresh one plainly it has no memory of the run and point it at the repo diff/commits instead of asking for done-done evidence cold.' Alternatively fold a one-line push-back into the existing maintainer Push-back-moves list.
